text:
Alice: quick follow-up from the Triton vs CUTLASS RFC — want to capture experiment matrix + owners so we can move to hands-on proofs this sprint. tl;dr: we need concrete perf + memory + maintenance signals, not just toy numbers.

Ben: +1. I sketched an experiment matrix earlier today. posting high-level here and asking for owners for each cell.

Carla: can you paste the matrix? I want to check coverage for long-seq workloads (2k+)

Ben: matrix (rows = kernel impl, cols = workload dims):
- kernels: triton-custom, cutlass-lower-level, cutlass-epilogue-optimized, legacy-cublas-ffi
- seq lens: 32, 128, 512, 2048
- batch sizes: 1, 8, 32
- precisions: fp16, int8/nf4
- models: causal-gpt (1B, 7B), encoder-decoder (t5-xxl-ish), llama-like 13B
- hw: A100(40GB), H100(80GB), V100(32GB) when possible
- metrics: p50/p90/p99 latency, tokens/sec, peak GPU memory, KV-cache footprint, compile time, kernel-init JIT time, maintainability notes (lines changed, third-party deps)

Devon: that looks good. add an availability/fallback column: how often we need to fallback to a slower kernel during a mixed workload run.

Ben: added. also adding an "integration cost" quick score for driver/runtime complexity.

Elliot: who owns running these on H100? I can do A100 batch runs but I don't have direct H100 access in my quota.

Ben: @Elliot — can you own A100 + functional harness? @Ben will own H100 runs (I have credits).

Carla: I'll own long-seq (2048) + encoder-decoder runs — those stress KV-cache and attention memory patterns.

Alice: I'll do the maintainability/ops side: prototype the kernel-switch registry API and the fallback shim. want a minimal config schema like:
{
  "kernel_order": ["triton", "cutlass"],
  "fallback": "cutlass",
  "compat_rules": {
    "max_seq_len": 2048,
    "precision": ["fp16", "int8"]
  }
}
We'll use this as the contract for runtime selection during experiments.

Devon: make sure the registry includes a "safety" flag so experiments can opt-out of autoscaling channels that expect stricter latency SLOs.

infra-bot: nightly-harness scheduled: perfbench.yaml -> triggers at 02:00 UTC, duration: 6h, owners: ben, elliot

Ben: sample perf command I plan to run:
./perfbench.py --model gpt-7b --kernel triton --seq 512 --batch 8 --precision fp16 --hw h100 --out results/triton_7b_512b8.json

echo-bot: Note: remember to wipe model cache between runs to avoid KV cache leakage affecting results.

Carla: question about CUTLASS path: do we test both the epilogue-optimized kernels and the straightforward Cutlass GEMM path? they have different memory behaviors.

Ben: yes, both. label them cutlass-ep and cutlass-gemm in results.

Elliot: timeline proposal: 3 weeks for PoC + data, week 4: review and decision. Is everyone OK?

Alice: yes. decision rules we agreed earlier still apply: prefer the kernel that wins on p99 and reduces memory pressure without increasing tail latency regressions in mixed workloads. If two are similar, favor maintainability and simpler runtime integration.

Devon: action items (I'll track):
- Ben: run H100 matrix + upload raw JSONs (due: +10 days)
- Elliot: run A100 matrix + validate harness (due: +9 days)
- Carla: long-seq encoder-decoder runs + craft KV-cache microbench (due: +12 days)
- Alice: implement kernel registry prototype + fallback shim, add safety opt-out toggles (due: +7 days)
- Devon: prepare dashboard template (p50/p90/p99, mem, fallback-rate) and hook to results (due: +14 days)

Ben: note on perf anomalies: during earlier runs Triton had faster p50 but p99 varied wildly for 2k seq on A100. Might be compilation/JIT issues that stabilize after warmup. We'll include cold vs warm runs.

Carla: good call. include cold-warm columns: first 200 tokens vs steady-state.

Elliot: also measure kernel compile times and dynamic memory alloc spikes. compile-time can be huge for Triton generated kernels if we recompile per-size.

Alice: for integration tests I'm going to add a thin adapter interface in runtime:
class KernelImpl:
  def init(self, model_meta):
    ...
  def run(self, inputs, kv_cache):
    ...
  def supports(self, meta) -> bool:
    ...
Adapters must implement this and register at startup. That keeps runtime fallback trivial.

Devon: perfect. also add telemetry hooks: kernel_id, compile_time_ms, fallback_trigger_count.

Ben: one more practical: ensure we run mixed concurrency profiles (10 concurrent small requests + one large seq). That's where we've seen real regressions.

Carla: will add mixed-concurrency scenarios to my long-seq harness.

Alice: scheduling: let's review initial results in architecture sync on Tue (2026-04-07 16:00 UTC). if any owner is blocked before then ping in this thread.

Ben: acked, I've reserved H100 time.

Elliot: ack. will create GH PR with perf harness changes and sample result parser.

Carla: ack — will add KV microbench to the repo under perf/kv_cache_tests.

Devon: I'll prep the dashboard and add a section for "regression alerts" so we can automatically flag if p99 increases by >15% from baseline.

Alice: thanks all. keeping this thread as canonical tracking for the experiment. please update when you finish runs. :rocket:

release-bot: Created epic KF-2345 "Triton vs Cutlass proof-of-work" and linked tasks.

Ben: uploaded first draft of A100 fp16 runs to s3://redwood-perf/triton-cutlass/2026-03-28/

Elliot: PR #402 added harness CI; tests are green but need infra creds for H100 integration.

Carla: started encoder-decoder run, will post results JSON when done.

Alice: end state we're looking for: clear winner or good reason to adopt mixed strategy + runtime fallback. either outcome is fine as long as we have data and a migration plan.

Ben: noted. will keep outputs minimal and machine-readable for the dashboard.

Devon: closing loop: next status ping in 5 days unless blockers arise.
